title: Friday Lemon Cake  (El pastel de limón de los viernes)

segments.t: A las nueve y media, en el rincón de la cafetería, Tessa sirve café recién hecho para la señorita Evelyn y Caleb mientras recuerdan las tardes de viernes de hace veinticinco años. Escucha primero.
So, Caleb, you are really staying in the courtyard to greet Owen at noon?
Yes, Tessa. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.
Owen will not walk out. He always acted tough for five seconds, then softened.
You still remember that after all these years?
Of course! Every Friday when he missed a piano note, he frowned at the wall.
How did you get him smiling again, Miss Evelyn?
His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with powdered sugar on top!
Oh! Yellow lemon glaze! We fought over the corner piece every single Friday!
Hold everything! What time is it right now? Nine thirty-five!
Tessa, please do not do extra work because of us.
Six yellow lemons are sitting in my basket right now. This kitchen was waiting for today!
Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!
Ahora recorramos la escena paso a paso.
So, Caleb, you are really staying in the courtyard to greet Owen at noon?
'¿Así que, Caleb, de verdad te quedas en el patio para recibir a Owen al mediodía?'
Yes, Tessa. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.
'Sí, Tessa. Incluso si se da media vuelta y sale directo otra vez por la verja.'
Owen will not walk out. He always acted tough for five seconds, then softened.
'Owen no se marchará. Siempre se hacía el duro cinco segundos y luego se ablandaba.'
You still remember that after all these years?
'¿Todavía recuerda eso después de todos estos años?'
Of course! Every Friday when he missed a piano note, he frowned at the wall.
'¡Por supuesto! Cada viernes, cuando fallaba una nota de piano, fruncía el ceño mirando a la pared.'
How did you get him smiling again, Miss Evelyn?
'¿Cómo lograba que volviera a sonreír, señorita Evelyn?'
His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with powdered sugar on top!
'¡Su abuelo cortaba pastel tibio de limón con azúcar glas por encima!'
Oh! Yellow lemon glaze! We fought over the corner piece every single Friday!
'¡Oh! ¡Glaseado amarillo de limón! ¡Nos peleábamos por el trozo de la esquina todos los viernes!'
Hold everything! What time is it right now? Nine thirty-five!
'¡Alto todo el mundo! ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo? ¡Las nueve y treinta y cinco!'
Tessa, please do not do extra work because of us.
'Tessa, por favor no te tomes trabajo extra por nuestra culpa.'
Six yellow lemons are sitting in my basket right now. This kitchen was waiting for today!
'Seis limones amarillos están en mi cesta ahora mismo. ¡Esta cocina estaba esperando el día de hoy!'
Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!
'¡Hornea muchos trozos de esquina, querida!'
Escuchemos de nuevo toda la conversación seguida.
So, Caleb, you are really staying in the courtyard to greet Owen at noon?
Yes, Tessa. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.
Owen will not walk out. He always acted tough for five seconds, then softened.
You still remember that after all these years?
Of course! Every Friday when he missed a piano note, he frowned at the wall.
How did you get him smiling again, Miss Evelyn?
His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with powdered sugar on top!
Oh! Yellow lemon glaze! We fought over the corner piece every single Friday!
Hold everything! What time is it right now? Nine thirty-five!
Tessa, please do not do extra work because of us.
Six yellow lemons are sitting in my basket right now. This kitchen was waiting for today!
Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!
Seis limones frescos en la cesta de la cocina y dos horas hasta el mediodía: Tessa ya se ata el delantal. Salgamos al patio en la próxima escena.
Bye for now!
